limits: These26 ranges are decoded/inspected, not additional executed cases; snapshot copying and generic callback entry order are included.
The complete frame and its external consumers are not executed together.

shields: clock, duration, optional actor kinds and shield/exposure deadlines are variables
damage inputs are the prefix multiplier, incoming power and defense factor
sequences: dispatcher source damage/clock/height/angle roles are variables
whirlwind consumes current actor speed and clock
lines: dispatcher source damage/clock/height/angle roles are variables
charge40/.15/1000/u32upper/.2 and membership half/absolute mask are live constants
bombs: ordinary selector zero/unit initializers are live constants
waves: dispatcher source damage/clock/height and row distance/radii are variables
actions: shared hazard half constant controls both line width and cone/knockback epsilon
volleys: current speed/duration helpers execute their own constants
flight center/height/delay/counter and membership radius/distance are variable inputs
pools: dispatcher source damage/clock and area deadlines are variable inputs
actor_frame: elapsed/clock/player and native helper HP/damage outputs are variables
cast0/-1000/u32upper and guardianHP1 contexts are live constants
ward_hit_death: shared hit multiplier/power and HP are variables
ward defense begins at1, death clock comes fromGame+a4c, corpse cutoff1.2 is live
pull_teleport: source/player/angle/height/clock, ray result and zone index are variables
current clamp/collision/enqueue helpers execute their own constants

limits: Context ranges are decoded/inspected; they do not execute all of their caller bodies together. Variable fixture profiles are deliberate inputs, not claims that those values are hardcoded by the game.
Real collision fractions, height samples, trig/zone selection, packet serializers and publication are controlled seams; current clipping/clamping/queue helpers execute actual bytes.
Synthetic original-byte fixtures do not execute Rust or launch a reference/rebuilt game.
Visited instruction ranges include intercepted seam entrypoints; their bodies are not certified or counted as executed helpers. The inspected_frame_order group is decoded/static review only.
Terrain, CRT, packet/allocation, nested dispatcher, actor constructor and damage-call seams retain the explicit boundaries in each fixture.
Historical volley inputs retain their actual0.108.0 provenance; every current instruction/result is checked afresh.
Complete generic item/talent callback bodies and a whole shared actor frame are not executed together. Terrain, population cap and gameplay/rendering parity remain separate requirements.
